summary: Adversarial judgment pass completed over 12-page cross-generation sample of utilityexplained.com. Delivered Slop Verdict, Trust/E-E-A-T Verdict, Ranked Bounce Hypotheses, 5 Weakest Page Nominations, and Site Verdict. All claims rigorously tagged as OBSERVED (with quotes/paths), INFERENCE, or GAP.
findings: AI-Slop Severity is HIGH due to structural artifacts ('Phantom Philosophy' intros, 'Echo-Bloop' templates, algorithmic link-stuffing), though factual hallucinations are LOW.
Trust/E-E-A-T Rating is C+. Core citations (tariffs, DOE/EIA) are robust, but metadata reveals a 2025-12-25 batch launch followed by bulk timestamp manipulations (zombie content).
Bounce Rate (91%) is primarily driven by the 'Quick Answer' instant-satisfaction gap (users get the answer in 65s and leave), followed by hyperlink-induced cognitive friction.

The 5 Weakest Pages are: net-metering-explained.md (geographic bias), how-utility-rates-fees-usage-work-together.md (meaningless filler), which-rate-plan-is-right-for-me.md (dangerous oversimplification), average-utility-bills-by-state-2026.md (zero actionability), afue-vs-seer-vs-hspf-vs-cop.md (dry textbook abstraction).

risks: Batch metadata dates may trigger Search Console manual actions for deceptive freshness if not updated organically.
Ambiguous safety warnings (electrical/rate gambling) expose the publisher to liability risks outside typical informational guides.
unknowns: Whether Hugo theme layouts enforce the visual repetition programmatically or if authors are manually copying headers.
Exact affiliate conversion metrics to determine if the 'honesty-first' approach on monitor/review pages outperforms the 'quick-pivot' approach on diagnostic pages.
